title: Event Quality Gate and Adaptive Buffering for Console Usage Pipeline
creator: Sophie Chen
description: Summary: The console usage pipeline is experiencing intermittent drops and schema rejections during traffic spikes and rapid producer-side schema changes. This ticket proposes an Event Quality Gate (EQG) service placed in front of the existing ingest path that combines fast, non-blocking shape checks with an adaptive buffering layer to smooth bursts and enable a 'soft-accept' mode for safe schema evolution.
description_2:
Goals:
- Reduce hard rejections of valid-but-new event shapes by enabling soft-accept & tagging for 0-downtime schema evolution.
- Limit downstream overloads during bursts by buffering and applying backpressure when necessary.
- Preserve low p99 ingest latency for normal traffic (<150ms added tail).
- Provide clear observability (rejection rates, soft-accept trends, buffer fill) and a simple rollback path.
design_notes:
Placement: EQG runs as a horizontally scalable HTTP/GRPC proxy in the console backend cluster. Incoming events hit EQG first; EQG runs a lightweight shape fingerprint check (fast) and a deeper schema conformance step (async).
Validation model:
- Fast Path: fingerprint + whitelist map in local memcache for immediate accept/annotate.
- Soft-Accept Path: novel shapes up to configured threshold are accepted, enriched with a "soft_accept" header and forwarded; an async worker stores samples and triggers an alert to schema owners.
- Hard-Reject Path: known-invalid events are rejected with 4xx and a structured error payload.
Adaptive Buffering:
- Per-tenant in-memory ring buffer (configurable size) backed by Redis for spillover.
- Token-bucket rate smoothing to maintain steady write rate to downstream consumers.
- Circuit breaker: if downstream write errors exceed threshold for 30s, EQG flips tenant to buffering-only and responds with 202 + advisory header to producers.
Schema Evolution Workflow:
- Novel shapes sampled (with PII redaction) to s3://redwood-samples/usage/YYYY/MM/DD and a Confluence checklist auto-created.
- Owners get an aggregated diff and can approve, request changes, or mark as transient (auto-expunge after 72h).
Instrumentation:
- New metrics: eqg.ingest.latency.{p50,p95,p99}, eqg.soft_accept.rate, eqg.hard_reject.rate, eqg.buffer.fill_ratio, eqg.sampleed_shapes.count.
- Dashboards: console/usage-ingest-quality (Kibana) and alert rules for sustained soft_accept > 5% over 1h for high-volume tenants.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Soft-accept increases downstream schema heterogeneity; mitigated by explicit tagging and short TTL before enforcement.
- Buffering increases memory/latency; we cap per-tenant buffer and expose backpressure to producers.
- Adding a proxy hop could add latency; optimize fast path hot-cache and keep p99 impact <150ms.
- Sampling must avoid PII leakage; include mandatory PII redaction plugin before any persistence.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature-flagged EQG builds deployed to canary cluster.
2) Canary tenants (internal teams + two small customers) enabled with soft-accept and sampling only. Monitor for 72h.
3) Enable buffering for canary tenants and run chaos tests (downstream failures).
4) Gradually expand to 10% traffic, 25%, 50% with automated checks.
5) Full rollout if acceptance criteria met, otherwise rollback to previous ingest gateway.
Fallback: Route to legacy ingest gateway if EQG is unhealthy; health check returns 503 to route controller.
acceptance_criteria:
- Hard rejection rate for console usage events decreases by >=80% within canary cohort for novel producer schema changes.
- p99 ingest latency overhead compared to baseline is <150ms for 95% of tenants.
- Buffer-related data loss = 0 (no dropped events during controlled downstream failure tests).
- Alerting and sample collection produce actionable artifacts (samples appear in S3 + Confluence summary within 10m of first soft-accept).
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for fingerprinting and fast-path cache.
- Integration tests: simulated producer with evolving schema, verify soft-accept tagging and sample persistence.
- Performance tests: synthetic burst load to measure buffer and p99 impact.
- Chaos test: force downstream write errors and verify circuit-breaker behavior and no silent data loss.
- Security test: PII redaction verification and sample store access control audits.
implementation_todos:
- Build EQG proxy (Go) and shared shape-fingerprint library.
- Redis-backed spillover queue + per-tenant bounds.
- Async sampler worker and S3 persistence with encryption.
- Confluence automation to create sample review page + Slack alert integration.
- Add metrics & tracing (OpenTelemetry) and dashboards.
- Feature flag wiring in deploy pipeline and routing rules in traffic router.
comments: 2025-02-14 Sophie Chen: Initial draft and proposal. Collected examples of recent rejections from observability (see links).
2025-02-18 Marco Alvarez: Reviewed fast-path cache design; suggested adding LRU eviction and a per-tenant TTL for entries to avoid staleness.
2025-02-20 Priya Nair (PM): Requested explicit rollback criteria and a customer communications plan for soft-accept behavior.
2025-02-25 Daniel Park: Spike complete for adapter prototype (branch: github.com/redwood/eqg/spike). Prototype shows median added latency ~12ms; p99 at 180ms under current config. Need perf tuning.
2025-02-27 Security Team (Aisha Patel): Confirmed sampling pipeline must run redaction plugin; suggested adding KMS-encrypted S3 bucket and limited IAM role for sampler.

2025-03-01 Daniel Park: Started canary rollout for internal tenants. Observed soft_accept.rate = 2.1% and buffer.fill_ratio peaked at 0.42 for canary period. Posting dashboard: https://kibana.redwood.example/app/dashboards#/view/usage-ingest-quality
2025-03-02 Sophie Chen: Updated acceptance criteria after canary results; plan to tune token-bucket refill to reduce p99. Created PR: https://github.com/redwood/eqg/pull/42
